chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about Qunut in all five prayers, and he said, 'Perform Qunut in all of them.' I then asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said, 'As for what you recite aloud, do not doubt [its permissibility].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Qunut in the five daily prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the permissibility and recommendation of performing Qunut in all five daily prayers, reflecting the Shia view that it is a Sunnah Mu'akkadah rather than a mandatory act. The clarification regarding 'what you recite aloud' (amma ma jaharta bihi) specifically addresses the recitation of the supplication itself during the Fajr prayer, distinguishing it from the silent recitation of Surah Al-Fatiha, thereby resolving practical nuances in ritual performance.
